The uniqueness of the Aranmula kannadi is that it is front reflecting, unlike plane glass mirrors where reflection takes place on the back surface of the glass, where the reflective coating is applied.
An Aranmula Kannadi, by contrast, is a front-surface mirror. Its reflective surface is the polished metal itself.
This gives the mirror its characteristic clarity and eliminates the secondary reflection associated with conventional glass mirrors.
In plane mirrors, light travels through the glass and back, so it gets refracted and changes direction. This can cause aberration or distortion of the image
The metal mirrors, unlike modern coated glass mirrors, have the property of 'point image' due to absence of refraction through glass and specular reflection
